newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Minsur tin plant start-up seen.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Minsur tin plant start-up seen.

text.p: The Minsur SA tin smelter in Peru has started production of nominal amounts of tin ahead of its planned commissioning next month, its Australian project engineering manager, Ausmelt Ltd, said on Monday.
The project, located 240 km south of Lima, originally was scheduled to start production about a year ago, eventually building to annual capacity output of some 20,000 tonnes a year.

However, technical and infrastructure problems extended the development period, Paul Abbott, Ausmelt's company secretary told Reuters. Minsur is using Ausmelt technology for the first time in a greenfield tin smelter project. The technology failed when grafted on to an existing tin smelter in the past.
Abbott said about 200 tonnes of tin produced at the smelter had been shipped to Britain. An official commissioning of the plant was expected to take place in October, he said.
The smelter will initially have capacity to treat 30,000 tonnes of concentrate feed, producing 15,466 tonnes of tin, grading 99.9 percent.
In about three years, the smelter's output could be raised to 20,600 tonnes a year, requiring about 40,000 tonnes of concentrate, Abbott said.
This would be accomplished using an oxygen-enrichmnebnt process, he said.
Ausmelt linked its A$3.1 million net loss in 1995/1996 (June 30) to problems in bringing the Minsur smelter and other greenfield projects on line.
